Voiceless plosive; 'in most environments' the alveolar ridge 'receives tongue-blade contact even while the tongue tip makes contact at some place on the teeth' (p. 151). Ellis's 'dental-alveolar' column, which he uses for t, n, r, s and l in all four languages (p. 145). Table 3-8 (p. 152).

Voiced labialized and velarized bilabial plosive, spelled bw; the only SpnCRL consonant matching none of Woleaian, Satawalese and Puluwatese, 'innovated' where Satawalese and Puluwatese keep the voiceless pʷˠ of Proto-Chuukic (pp. 156-158). Its geminate is the voiceless pʷː (Table 3-11). Ellis writes it with superscript ʷ and ˠ (labialized and velarized, as Roddy 2007 does for Satawalese); entered with ʷ as in the other Chuukic lects (decision ellis2012-symbols). Table 3-8 (p. 152).

Geminate of bʷ, in parentheses in Table 3-8 because its place in the chart differs from the single form's ('(bʷˠ:) --> pʷˠ:', Table 3-11). Spelled pw, which 'represents doubled /bw/' (Jackson & Marck 1991: 27, 365). Ellis writes it with superscript ʷ and ˠ (labialized and velarized, as Roddy 2007 does for Satawalese); entered with ʷ as in the other Chuukic lects (decision ellis2012-symbols). Table 3-8 (p. 152).

Geminate retroflex affricate, spelled tch ('represents doubled /sch/', Jackson & Marck 1991: 452): the geminate of ʂ (Table 3-8, '(ʂ:) --> ʈʂ͡:ʲ', Table 3-11). Ellis writes ʈʂ͡:ʲ, 'retroflexed and palatalized', with the same symbol as Woleaian ch, whose tongue position he leaves open (pp. 145, 151); there is no single form. Entered as ʈ͡ʂː (decision ellis2012-symbols). Table 3-8 (p. 152).

Geminate velar plosive, also the geminate of x ('(x:) --> k:', Table 3-11). Like Woleaian, SpnCRL lacks a single k (p. 158); k is 'not found singly in native words' (Jackson & Marck 1991: 229). Table 3-8 (p. 152).
